tasks.short: Agree practical inclusion support with community partners under applicable programme requirements.

steps.what: Read programme requirements, existing agreements and partner information.

loop.input: Approved programme requirements and existing agreement.
loop.output: Requirements brief with source passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate source references; officer checks obligations and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting text goes to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Programme obligations appear in varied prose; fixed fields cannot reliably capture their conditions.

steps.what: Discuss community needs, practical barriers and possible support.
Approve support scope, resources and limits on commitments.
Draft assistance terms, responsibilities, milestones and reporting arrangements.

loop.input: Approved scope, cited requirements and approved agreement template.
loop.output: Draft assistance agreement with departures and missing terms marked.
loop.check: Check mandatory sections, scope consistency and references; officer reviews the draft.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved obligations remain marked for legal review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard clauses, but partner responsibilities and support arrangements need tailored wording.

steps.what: Review legal obligations, funding conditions and proposed terms before circulation.
Negotiate remaining terms with the community partner.
Approve final commitments and sign the assistance agreement.
Record the signed agreement and schedule responsibilities and review dates.

tasks.design: A controlled workspace in the {CLM} uses templates from the {DOCS}, with bounded extraction and drafting loops for programme requirements and tailored terms. The {WORKFLOW} routes clearance, material departures and final approval, while the {ESIGN} records signatures and creates milestones in the {PROJECT}. Consultation and negotiation stay with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Partner needs and programme conditions differ. Templates already help, but assembling requirements and tailored terms still takes manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small document workflow cheaper to build. Bounded text extraction and drafting can reduce preparation when source documents and templates are controlled.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, competing expectations and legal interpretation remain human work. GDPR governs any personal data shared; EU AI Act applicability depends on the actual use, and national rules may add consultation requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whose needs are missing, build trust and negotiate commitments the organisation can honour.

ambition.what: A partner-led clinic helping applicants request accessible recruitment arrangements.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling agreements and more time shaping practical support with partners. They gain scope to propose the clinic; budget and binding commitments still require approval.

reach.task: Design briefing sessions for staff delivering the agreed support.
reach.learn: Learn accessible instruction, learning objectives and how to check whether staff can apply the agreement.

evidence.claim: Community consultation and negotiation require human judgement; preparation, templates and milestone routing can be supported separately.
A documented government report contained invented sources and led to partial repayment; generated agreement references therefore need verification.
The proposed build ranges and remaining time percentages are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This supplemental task occurs when the employer joins a community inclusion or publicly supported employment programme.
The employer negotiates its own assistance commitments and does not exercise a government's enforcement powers.
Agreements use approved templates, with legal review available.
Preparation and administration are smaller than consultation and negotiation, consistent with the supplied priors.
Consent and access estimates include conditional employee consultation under national rules; statutory processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which programmes, funding conditions and national rules apply.
Which roles can approve expenditure, terms and signatures.
Whether existing agreement templates and system workflows cover this work.
Whether agreements contain sensitive personal data or require partner data sharing.
Whether employee representatives must be consulted about the proposed processing.
research_questions: Which programme clauses are mandatory, and which can use approved alternatives?
Can approved agreement fields populate milestones without extracting the signed document again?
What validation catches omitted conditions in a sample of past agreements?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and tailored draft terms.
Maintain approved templates and source versions.
Route material negotiated departures back through legal and budget approval.
Handle failed signature routing and incorrect milestone assignments.
Maintain restricted access and retention for partner records.

tasks.short: Help plan and deliver inclusive recruitment events and advertising.

steps.what: Review vacancies, previous outreach results and known accessibility barriers.
Choose events, audiences, accessibility arrangements and advertising budget.
Prepare inclusive event materials and recruitment advertising copy.

loop.input: Approved vacancy facts, outreach plan, templates and accessibility guidance.
loop.output: Draft adverts and event materials with factual references.
loop.check: Check required fields, vacancy facts and unsupported promises; officer reviews language and accessibility.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per format; unresolved claims return to the recruiter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but channel wording and explanations of support vary.

steps.what: Coordinate organisers, staffing, equipment and accessible event arrangements.
Approve and publish recruitment adverts and event information.
Meet potential applicants, explain vacancies and discuss recruitment accessibility.
Record candidate contact requests and communication preferences.
Send requested vacancy information and application links.
Compare outreach results and identify improvements for the next event.

tasks.design: Use the {ATS} for event registration and requested follow-up, with an outreach dashboard in the {BI} and configured logistics in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded drafting loop uses approved material from the {DOCS}; the recruitment manager approves publication through the {ATS}, {CMS} or {ADS}. The officer continues applicant conversations and interprets outreach results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event logistics, candidate follow-up and results often sit in separate tools. Copy varies by channel, while small event volumes can make bespoke integrations uneconomic.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing registration, notification and approval features can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort for missing connections, and bounded drafting helps adapt approved copy.
tasks.still_hard: Event attendance does not establish equal opportunity or explain recruitment outcomes. GDPR limits collection and reuse of sensitive data; EU AI Act obligations require separate assessment if the scope expands to applicant screening or evaluation, and national rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Make applicants feel welcome, understand barriers they disclose and explain realistic routes into employment.

ambition.what: Reach applicants needing accessible recruitment formats through a community career event.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time preparing packs and chasing logistics, leaving more time for applicant conversations and accessibility follow-up. They can recommend channel and format changes after each event; budget and publication approval stay with the recruitment manager.

reach.task: Manage the transition from event enquiry to recruitment application.
reach.learn: Learn registration design, communication preferences, source attribution and accessible application handoffs.

evidence.claim: Recruitment systems commonly support contact records and templated messages; availability depends on configuration and access.
Deterministic reporting can assemble outreach counts; interpreting accessibility barriers and selecting channels still requires judgement.
The proposed build ranges and remaining time percentages are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The officer participates alongside recruiters rather than owning the entire recruitment campaign.
Face-to-face outreach remains the largest single activity, consistent with the supplied priors.
Channel and event attribution can use operational data without inferring protected characteristics.
Candidates can enter their own contact requests through an accessible registration form.
Automatic messages contain requested, approved information and do not make selection decisions.
Consent and access estimates include conditional employee consultation under national rules; statutory processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which registration, messaging and publication features existing systems provide.
How event enquiries are recorded today and whether paper registration remains necessary.
Which channels, budgets and external bookings the officer may authorise.
Which candidate data can lawfully be collected and retained.
Whether outcome attribution is reliable enough for channel comparisons.
Which employee consultation and accessibility requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing registration features support accessible self-entry and the required privacy notice?
Which outreach measures remain useful when event volumes are small?
Can approved adverts publish through existing connectors without a custom integration?
How should accommodation requests reach a restricted human support route?
new_work: Review generated materials for accuracy, accessibility and unsupported promises.
Handle unusual organiser requests and event booking exceptions.
Maintain templates, publication permissions and registration forms.
Resolve duplicate contact records and failed requested messages.
Check attribution quality and prevent disclosure through small reporting groups.

role.altitude: The role shifts some effort from paperwork and coordination to partner relationships, accessible recruitment and practical interventions. The officer gains better evidence for recommendations; legal, budget and employment decision rights do not automatically expand.
reach: Help human resources specialists improve event-to-application handoffs.
Help training and development specialists prepare staff to deliver agreed inclusion support.
skills_to_grow: Interpreting aggregate outreach evidence without overstating causation.
Reviewing generated text against approved sources.
Privacy-aware workflow design and exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Build a community inclusion service combining partner agreements, accessible recruitment events and practical applicant support, with human-led consultation and clear approval limits.
